title: A Hidden Shame in Nursing Homes

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是安德鲁·罗斯-索金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at the
sentences.zh: 我负责《纽约时报》每日简报 DealBook 的商业与政策报道。

sentences.en: New York Times.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市 DealBook 峰会的现场采访一些商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的领袖，包括 J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜

sentences.en: Lagarde, Zylran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼以及许多其他人。

sentences.zh: 你可以直接观看其中一些毫无保留、未经过滤的现场对话。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望大家准时收看。

sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Bilbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是来自《纽约时报》的迈克尔·比尔巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这里是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Today.
sentences.zh: 今天是。

sentences.en: A Times investigation finds that nursing homes across the U.S.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的一项调查发现，全美各地的养老院

sentences.en: are diagnosing and treating their elderly residents for schizophrenia at alarmingly high rates, even when there's no evidence of the illness.
sentences.zh: 正以惊人的高比例诊断和治疗老年居民的的精神分裂症，即使根本没有患病迹象也是如此。

sentences.en: I spoke to my colleague, Katie Thomas, about the government loophole that allowed it to happen.
sentences.zh: 我与我的同事凯蒂·托马斯聊了聊导致这种情况发生的政府漏洞。

sentences.en: It's Tuesday, September 14th.
sentences.zh: 今天是9月14日，星期二。

sentences.en: Katie, tell me about
sentences.zh: 凯蒂，跟我讲讲

sentences.en: David Blakeney.
sentences.zh: 大卫·布莱克尼。

sentences.en: What I know about David Blakeney...
sentences.zh: 我对大卫·布莱克尼的了解……

sentences.en: How long were you two married?
sentences.zh: 你们俩结婚多久了？

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: ...is through his wife of 42 years, Yvonne Blakeney.
sentences.zh: ……是通过他结婚42年的妻子伊冯娜·布莱克尼了解到的。

sentences.en: And she lives in South Carolina.
sentences.zh: 她住在南卡罗来纳州。

sentences.en: And how did you guys meet?
sentences.zh: 你们俩是怎么认识的？

sentences.en: Oh, okay.
sentences.zh: 噢，好的。

sentences.en: That was way back in the 70s.
sentences.zh: 那得追溯到20世纪70年代。

sentences.en: And she told me that they met through family.
sentences.zh: 她告诉我，他们是通过家人认识的。

sentences.en: And at the time, she had four young children.
sentences.zh: 当时，她有四个年幼的孩子。

sentences.en: One was just a baby.
sentences.zh: 其中一个还是婴儿。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: So that is a lot of work.
sentences.zh: 所以那有相当多繁重的工作。

sentences.en: What drew her to him was that he said he would take care of them.
sentences.zh: 吸引她的是他说过他会照顾他们。

sentences.en: He would take care of her and the children.
sentences.zh: 他会照顾她和孩子们。

sentences.en: And he did.
sentences.zh: 他也确实做到了。

sentences.en: They spent the next 40 years together.
sentences.zh: 他们在接下来的40年里一直度过。

sentences.en: And he raised those kids as if they were his own.
sentences.zh: 他把那些孩子抚养长大，就像亲生的一样。

sentences.en: And tell me just more about him.
sentences.zh: 能多跟我讲讲他吗？

sentences.en: You know, what was he like?
sentences.zh: 你知道，他是个什么样的人？

sentences.en: He worked for four decades as a farmhand.
sentences.zh: 他当了四十年的农场帮工。

sentences.en: And she said he was a big, muscular guy.
sentences.zh: 她说他是个身材魁梧的壮汉。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: When he was like a young man, 250 pounds.
sentences.zh: 他年轻时，有250磅重。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: She said, you know, he once thought nothing of just scrambling up on the tops of those big irrigation rigs to fix something and then right back down.
sentences.zh: 她说，你知道，他以前觉得三两下爬到那些大灌溉机顶上去修东西，然后马上下来根本不算什么。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: You know, so he worked hard for most of his life.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他大半辈子都在努力工作。

sentences.en: But when he was in his early 60s, his health just started declining.
sentences.zh: 但当他刚满60岁时，他的健康状况开始恶化。

sentences.en: And he developed dementia.
sentences.zh: 他患上了痴呆症。

sentences.en: He became increasingly confused, forgetful.
sentences.zh: 他变得越来越糊涂、健忘。

sentences.en: He would wander out of the house.
sentences.zh: 他会从家里走失。

sentences.en: People would bring him back home.
sentences.zh: 人们会把他送回家。

sentences.en: He got so bad, you know.
sentences.zh: 情况变得很糟糕，你知道的。

sentences.en: Ms. Blake Neaverly struggled to take care of him.
sentences.zh: 布莱克尼夫人竭力照顾他。

sentences.en: And eventually she just, you know, to her own heartbreak, she concluded that she couldn't care for him herself.
sentences.zh: 最终她，带着心碎，断定自己无法独自照顾他。

sentences.en: And so she brought him to a nursing home in South Carolina in October of 2016.
sentences.zh: 于是，她在2016年10月把他送到了南卡罗来纳州的一家养老院。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: So at this facility, she was really shocked at how quickly he declined.
sentences.zh: 所以在该机构，他恶化的速度让她大吃一惊。

sentences.en: He was sleeping all of the time.
sentences.zh: 他一直在睡觉。

sentences.en: I got pictures of him in my phone where I would take him and he'd be sitting up in that wheelchair sleep.
sentences.zh: 我的手机里有他的照片，我带他去的时候，他坐在轮椅上睡着了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: That was faSt.
sentences.zh: 那太快了。

sentences.en: You know, even when she brought his favorite meals, he wouldn't wake up.
sentences.zh: 你知道，甚至当她带来他最喜欢的饭菜时，他也不会醒来。

sentences.en: He just kept losing weight, kept losing weight.
sentences.zh: 他一直在消瘦，一直在消瘦。

sentences.en: She started to see, you know, this once robust man.
sentences.zh: 她开始看到，曾经健壮的这个人。

sentences.en: She could see his ribs sticking out.
sentences.zh: 她能看到他的肋骨凸显出来。

sentences.en: And, you know, he developed bed sores because he was just always in his bed or in his wheelchair asleep.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，他生了褥疮，因为他总是躺在床上或坐在轮椅上睡觉。

sentences.en: And I went one day and I seen his, you know, how his foot was looking, you know, like it wasn't right.
sentences.zh: 有一天我去的时候，我看到了他的，你知道的，他的脚看起来是什么样子的，你知道的，就好像不太对劲。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: Several months after he arrived, he actually had to have one of his feet amputated because the bed sores got so bad.
sentences.zh: 他入住几个月后，由于褥疮实在太严重，实际上不得不截肢了一只脚。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: And then by eight months after he was at the facility, he went from over 200 pounds to 128 pounds.
sentences.zh: 接着在他入住该机构八个月后，他的体重从200多磅降到了128磅。

sentences.en: And eventually he died.
sentences.zh: 最后他去世了。

sentences.en: His death shattered his family and they were heartbroken.
sentences.zh: 他的死击碎了他的家庭，他们悲痛欲绝。

sentences.en: But Mrs. Blakeney was also really upset about the way he had been cared for in the last eight months of his life.
sentences.zh: 但布莱克尼夫人对他在生命最后八个月受到的照料方式也感到非常不满。

sentences.en: She had seen what had happened to him and how quickly he had declined.
sentences.zh: 她亲眼目睹了发生在他身上的事情以及他恶化的速度有多快。

sentences.en: And she felt like he hadn't been treated well there.
sentences.zh: 她觉得他在那里没有得到良好的对待。

sentences.en: And she wanted answers and accountability from the nursing home.
sentences.zh: 她希望养老院能给她一个说法并追究责任。

sentences.en: So she hired a lawyer to sue the nursing home.
sentences.zh: 于是她雇了一名律师起诉这家养老院。

sentences.en: And it was only after she hired the lawyer that she learned something that really shocked her,
sentences.zh: 正是雇了律师之后，她才得知了一件让她大吃一惊的事，

sentences.en: which was that while he was in the nursing home, he was receiving a powerful antipsychotic drug.
sentences.zh: 那就是当他在养老院时，他一直在服用强效抗精神病药物。

sentences.en: And not only that, but he had a diagnosis of schizophrenia.
sentences.zh: 不仅如此，他还被诊断患有精神分裂症。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: And why was that so shocking to her?
sentences.zh: 为什么这让她如此震惊？

sentences.en: Well, because she had been married to him and known him for more than 40 years.
sentences.zh: 嗯，因为她嫁给他并认识他已经超过40年了。

sentences.en: And schizophrenia is something that is usually diagnosed in young adulthood.
sentences.zh: 而精神分裂症通常是在成年早期就被诊断出来的。

sentences.en: And there had never been any evidence that he had had schizophrenia or any other serious mental illness, you know.
sentences.zh: 并且从来没有任何证据表明他曾患有精神分裂症或其他任何严重的精神疾病，你知道的。

sentences.en: So to see that he had been diagnosed with this at the end of his life came as a surprise to her and just didn't seem right to her.
sentences.zh: 所以看到他在生命尽头被诊断出这个病，她感到很意外，也觉得很不合理。

sentences.en: So what exactly is happening here?
sentences.zh: 那么这里到底发生了什么？

sentences.en: Well, what happened to David Blakeney has been happening to nursing home residents for over 50 years,
sentences.zh: 嗯，大卫·布莱克尼身上发生的事，在养老院居民身上已经上演了50多年，

sentences.en: where nursing homes have been giving these antipsychotic drugs to dementia patients as an effort to control their behavior.
sentences.zh: 养老院一直给痴呆症患者服用这些抗精神病药物，以此来控制他们的行为。

sentences.en: And when you say control their behavior, what do you mean?
sentences.zh: 当你说的控制他们的行为时，是什么意思？

sentences.en: Well, you know, they've really been leaned on by the doctors and nursing homes to effectively kind of sedate them and to kind of make them easier to deal with.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道的，医生和养老院确实一直在向他们施压，实际上是为了起到镇静作用，让他们更容易对付。

sentences.en: You know, some dementia patients have some really, really challenging behaviors.
sentences.zh: 你知道，一些痴呆症患者有一些非常、非常具有挑战性的行为。

sentences.en: You know, they can wander.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们会到处乱跑。

sentences.en: They can become agitated.
sentences.zh: 他们会变得烦躁不安。

sentences.en: They can strike out at staff and residents.
sentences.zh: 他们会袭击工作人员和其他居民。

sentences.en: And it's a really hard thing to manage, especially if you don't have the resources and the staff to deal with it.
sentences.zh: 这是个很难处理的问题，尤其是如果你没有资源和人手来应对的话。

sentences.en: And so for a very long time, some nursing homes and the doctors that prescribe these drugs have used them as almost like a shortcut or a crutch
sentences.zh: 所以在很长一段时间里，一些养老院和开具这些药物的医生几乎把它们当作捷径或拐杖，

sentences.en: in order to make it easier to care for these patients.
sentences.zh: 以便更容易地照顾这些病人。

sentences.en: Almost sedating people into submission.
sentences.zh: 几乎是用镇静剂让人顺从。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And during all these decades that nursing homes have been doing this, has this been an acceptable and understood protocol?
sentences.zh: 在养老院这样做长达几十年的时间里，这一直是一个被接受且被理解的规程吗？

sentences.en: Well, it's certainly been a widespread practice.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这无疑是一种广泛存在的做法。

sentences.en: Very, very common in nursing homes.
sentences.zh: 在养老院非常、非常普遍。

sentences.en: But almost as soon as it became widespread, there was also pushback against it.
sentences.zh: 但几乎在它变得普遍的同时，也有人对其进行抵制。

sentences.en: And people asking if this was the right thing to do.
sentences.zh: 人们质疑这到底是不是正确的做法。

sentences.en: You know, there's a number of reasons to be concerned about it.
sentences.zh: 你知道，有许多理由让人对此感到担忧。

sentences.en: It can deprive people of their dignity to basically control them, perhaps against their will.
sentences.zh: 这可能会剥夺人们的尊严，基本上是去控制他们，也许是违背他们的意愿。

sentences.en: If you sedate someone, it can be harmful to their health, right?
sentences.zh: 如果你给某人服用镇静剂，这对他们的健康有害，对吧？

sentences.en: They can be more likely to fall.
sentences.zh: 他们更有可能跌倒。

sentences.en: They can develop bed sores.
sentences.zh: 他们可能会生褥疮。

sentences.en: They don't eat.
sentences.zh: 他们不吃饭。

sentences.en: They can lose weight.
sentences.zh: 他们会体重减轻。

sentences.en: They can become dehydrated.
sentences.zh: 他们会脱水。

sentences.en: There's all sorts of medical reasons why it's bad for them.
sentences.zh: 有各种各样的医学原因表明这对他们有害。

sentences.en: And it's also why it's been called by doctors and government officials and others who have objected to it, a chemical straitjacket.
sentences.zh: 这也是为什么它被反对它的医生、政府官员和其他人称为“化学直筒约束衣”。

sentences.en: And, you know, in the 1970s, there was a congressional investigation and a report that outlined, you know, the harms of using these drugs in nursing homes.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，在20世纪70年代，曾有过一次国会调查和报告，概述了在养老院使用这些药物的危害。

sentences.en: And then in the 1980s, President Reagan passed a law that essentially barred the use of any drug in a nursing home if it was what they called a chemical restraint,
sentences.zh: 然后到了20世纪80年代，里根总统通过了一项法律，基本上禁止在养老院使用任何被他们称为化学约束的药物，

sentences.en: which they defined as a drug that was being given to somebody to meet the needs of the staff that was taking care of them instead of treating the patient himself or herself.
sentences.zh: 他们将其定义为为了迎合照顾他们的员工的需求，而不是为了治疗患者本人而给某人服用的药物。

sentences.en: And does that law work?
sentences.zh: 那项法律管用吗？

sentences.en: Well, despite the law, the problem persisted.
sentences.zh: 嗯，尽管有这项法律，问题依然存在。

sentences.en: And the Food and Drug Administration in 2005 put a warning on antipsychotic drugs and told doctors that there was nearly double the risk of death in older dementia patients for antipsychotics,
sentences.zh: 美国食品药品监督管理局（FDA）在2005年对抗精神病药物发出了警告，并告诉医生，老年痴呆症患者服用抗精神病药物的死亡风险几乎翻了一番，

sentences.en: which was kind of an unusual warning because there's no FDA approval for antipsychotics in older dementia patients.
sentences.zh: 这算是一个不同寻常的警告，因为FDA并未批准抗精神病药物用于老年痴呆症患者。

sentences.en: So it was also a nod to the fact that these drugs were being widely prescribed, you know, outside of their approved use.
sentences.zh: 所以这也是在暗示这样一个事实：这些药物在获批用途之外被广泛开具，你知道的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And a nod to the fact that that Reagan era law probably hadn't really done its job.
sentences.zh: 这也暗示了里根时期的那项法律可能并没有真正发挥作用。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's right.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实如此。

sentences.en: And then years go by and the problem is still bad enough that by 2012, there's a new groundswell to do something about this issue.
sentences.zh: 随后几年过去了，问题依然严重，到2012年，又涌现出了一股新浪潮，要采取行动解决这个问题。

sentences.en: And so the idea that they come up with this time is to require nursing homes to report how many of their residents are taking these drugs.
sentences.zh: 所以他们这次想出的主意是，要求养老院报告有多少居民正在服用这些药物。

sentences.en: And the idea there is transparency, you know,
sentences.zh: 这背后的理念是透明度，你知道的，

sentences.en: that any member of the public or the government could rely on these statistics in order to kind of evaluate whether a nursing home was a good place to put their loved one.
sentences.zh: 任何公众或政府成员都可以依靠这些统计数据来评估养老院是否是安置其亲人的好地方。

sentences.en: So the logic is disclosure would discourage nursing homes from abusing these drugs.
sentences.zh: 所以其逻辑是信息披露将阻止养老院滥用这些药物。

sentences.en: Yes, that was the plan.
sentences.zh: 是的，这就是计划。

sentences.en: But in doing so, the government created a pretty big loophole.
sentences.zh: 但这样做时，政府留下了一个相当大的漏洞。

sentences.en: And that loophole was that nursing homes wouldn't have to disclose people who are using the drugs if they had a small list of conditions.
sentences.zh: 这个漏洞就是，如果养老院拥有一份很短的病情列表，他们就不必披露正在使用这些药物的人。

sentences.en: And one of those conditions was schizophrenia.
sentences.zh: 而这些病情之一就是精神分裂症。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: And that might create a different incentive structure, potentially, which is it would allow nursing homes to diagnose people with schizophrenia and never have to report it,
sentences.zh: 这可能会产生一种潜在的不同激励结构，也就是它将允许养老院诊断患者患有精神分裂症却永远不必上报，

sentences.en: which might lead to people diagnosing schizophrenia maybe when it's not there.
sentences.zh: 这可能会导致在根本没有精神分裂症的时候也诊断出该病。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: If they had a schizophrenia diagnosis, then it could potentially justify their use.
sentences.zh: 如果他们有了精神分裂症的诊断，那么这就能潜在地证明他们使用药物的合理性。

sentences.en: And that patient wouldn't be counted and wouldn't have to be reported in the public data.
sentences.zh: 并且该患者将不会被统计在内，也不必在公开数据中进行报告。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So what happens after this 2012 effort with this very big loophole is put into place?
sentences.zh: 那么在这个漏洞百出的2012年举措实施之后，发生了什么？

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: So even though these diagnoses are supposed to be excluded, you know, we got curious about what the number would be if they weren't.
sentences.zh: 所以，尽管这些诊断本应被排除在外，你知道，我们很好奇如果不排除的话，这个数字会是多少。

sentences.en: And so we wanted to investigate exactly that.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们想要对此展开深入调查。

sentences.en: And after a little bit of digging around, we found that since 2012, the number of nursing home residents who were diagnosed with schizophrenia has soared by 70%.
sentences.zh: 经过一番深入挖掘，我们发现自 2012 年以来，被诊断患有精神分裂症的疗养院居民人数激增了 70%。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: It's a huge increase.
sentences.zh: 这是一个巨大的增长。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: And, you know, to put that into perspective, that's one out of nine nursing home residents.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，换位思考一下，这意味着每九个疗养院居民中就有一个。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Now, I mean, there could be some reasons why there would be more patients with schizophrenia in nursing homes,
sentences.zh: 现在，我的意思是，疗养院中精神分裂症患者增多可能有一些原因，

sentences.en: but we found lots of other evidence that these false diagnoses were helping to drive this increase.
sentences.zh: 但我们发现了许多其他证据，表明这些错误的诊断正在推动这一增长。

sentences.en: And just to compare that to the general population, the best estimates are that one in 150 people have schizophrenia.
sentences.zh: 与普通人口相比，根据最佳估计，每 150 人中就有一人患有精神分裂症。

sentences.en: Compared to one out of nine in these nursing homes.
sentences.zh: 而这些疗养院的比例则是九分之一。

sentences.en: Yes, that's right.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: And once we saw those numbers, we wanted to dig in more.
sentences.zh: 一旦我们看到这些数字，我们就想做进一步的挖掘。

sentences.en: And that's what led us to the Blakeney family.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们找到布莱克尼一家的原因。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用程序？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 解锁了？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to the Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 大家都知道，你需要订阅《时报》才能查阅所有报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore the Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但是，如果你能免费体验《时报》一个月，且无需输入信用卡，会怎么样呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download the New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你首次下载《纽约时报》应用程序时，你在该应用程序中的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 有一个月的时间可以突破付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to the New York Times, download the Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅《纽约时报》，请立即下载《时报》应用程序，即可获得 30 天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: You said that they never went over his medications with you?
sentences.zh: 你说过他们从未跟你商量过他的药物治疗方案？

sentences.en: He was so mad.
sentences.zh: 他气坏了。

sentences.en: And I would go see him every day and I ain't never seen nobody give him nothing.
sentences.zh: 我每天都去看他，从没看见任何人给他任何东西。

sentences.en: When he was woke, I fed him.
sentences.zh: 他醒着的时候，我喂他吃饭。

sentences.en: And when he was asleep, I didn't bother.
sentences.zh: 他睡着的时候，我没有去打扰他。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: I knew he was asleep a lot, you know, and I couldn't wake him up.
sentences.zh: 我知道他经常睡觉，你知道的，而且我叫不醒他。

sentences.en: But I thought, you know, he was just, you know, asleep, you know.
sentences.zh: 但我以为，你知道的，他只是，你知道的，睡着了。

sentences.en: I didn't know they was dumping him up like, you know, they was.
sentences.zh: 我不知道他们像这样把他喂得昏迷不醒。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Because there wasn't nothing wrong with him.
sentences.zh: 因为他一点毛病也没有。

sentences.en: He just had to mention all I knew.
sentences.zh: 他只需要提及我所知道的一切。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对的。

sentences.en: Katie, you had told us that the Blakeney family had a lot of questions about David's death.
sentences.zh: 凯蒂，你曾告诉我们，布莱克尼一家对大卫的死有很多疑问。

sentences.en: They had hired a lawyer and they had sued.
sentences.zh: 他们请了律师，并提起了诉讼。

sentences.en: So what exactly did they learn through that legal process?
sentences.zh: 那么，他们通过法律程序究竟了解到了什么？

sentences.en: So the lawyer got all of Mr. Blakeney's medical records.
sentences.zh: 所以律师拿到了布莱克尼先生所有的病历。

sentences.en: And then once he got them, he and his team started just going through them.
sentences.zh: 一旦拿到病历，他和他的团队就开始仔细审阅。

sentences.en: And one of the things that he learned was that Mr. Blakeney had been getting Haldol,
sentences.zh: 他了解到的情况之一是，布莱克尼先生一直在服用氟哌啶醇，

sentences.en: which is an old antipsychotic that dates to the 1960s that has long been used on nursing home patients to control their behavior.
sentences.zh: 这是一种可以追溯到 20 世纪 60 年代的旧抗精神病药物，长期以来一直用于控制疗养院病人的行为。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: And how long had David Blakeney been getting Haldol?
sentences.zh: 大卫·布莱克尼服用氟哌啶醇多久了？

sentences.en: Well, as the lawyer went back into his files, he found that, you know, off and on at different medical facilities, he had been getting Haldol as well as some other antipsychotics.
sentences.zh: 嗯，随着律师翻阅他的档案，他发现，你知道的，在大大小小的医疗机构里，他断断续续地一直在服用氟哌啶醇以及其他一些抗精神病药物。

sentences.en: You know, he was at a nursing home near his home in Lancaster, South Carolina, where he was getting Haldol and a doctor there had given him a diagnosis of schizophrenia as well,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他曾住在南卡罗来纳州兰开斯特家附近的一家疗养院里，在那里他一直在服用氟哌啶醇，那里的医生也给他诊断患有精神分裂症，

sentences.en: even though there's, you know, his lawyer has said that there is no evidence that he was ever evaluated for schizophrenia.
sentences.zh: 尽管，你知道的，他的律师说没有证据表明他曾接受过精神分裂症评估。

sentences.en: And, you know, then he went home, he lived with his wife for a time until, you know, his condition declined again and his wife felt she couldn't care for him.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，后来他回家了，和妻子住了一段时间，直到，你知道的，他的病情再次恶化，他妻子觉得自己无法照顾他。

sentences.en: He went into a hospital where he continued to get the drugs and where the hospital did not give him any diagnosis of schizophrenia.
sentences.zh: 他住进了一家医院，继续服用这些药物，医院也没有给他做出任何精神分裂症的诊断。

sentences.en: He had a lot of different diagnoses and conditions, but that was not on the liSt.
sentences.zh: 他有许多不同的诊断和病情，但那并不在名单上。

sentences.en: And then eventually he ended up at the nursing home, Dundee Manor, where he would then spend the last eight months of his life.
sentences.zh: 最后，他来到了邓迪庄园疗养院，在那里度过了他人生的最后八个月。

sentences.en: And it was there that, again, a doctor gave him a diagnosis of schizophrenia, despite the fact that, you know,
sentences.zh: 正是在那里，一位医生再次诊断他患有精神分裂症，尽管事实是，你知道的，

sentences.en: there was no evidence that he had ever had a psychiatric evaluation for the condition.
sentences.zh: 没有证据表明他曾因该病情接受过精神科评估。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: So two nursing homes are independently, but without any psychological evaluations that the lawyer can find,
sentences.zh: 所以两家疗养院在没有任何律师能找到的心理评估的情况下，独立地，

sentences.en: diagnosing him with schizophrenia and treating him with this very powerful antipsychotic Haldol.
sentences.zh: 诊断他患有精神分裂症，并用这种效力极强的抗精神病药物氟哌啶醇治疗他。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And, you know, it's also worth just mentioning again that schizophrenia is a lifelong condition.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，也值得再次提及的是，精神分裂症是一种终身疾病。

sentences.en: It's something that you get in early adulthood.
sentences.zh: 这是你在成年早期就会患上的疾病。

sentences.en: And, you know, in the medical records for Dundee Manor, the last nursing home, in his records, it says that he had an onset of schizophrenia while he was at the nursing home.
sentences.zh: 并且，你知道的，在最后一家疗养院邓迪庄园的病历中，记录显示他在疗养院期间发作了精神分裂症。

sentences.en: Which you're saying doesn't really make sense because that's not how schizophrenia works.
sentences.zh: 你这是在说这根本说不通，因为精神分裂症不是这样的。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: The medical experts that I spoke to said that an elderly person getting a new diagnosis of schizophrenia is just extremely uncommon.
sentences.zh: 我交谈过的医学专家表示，老年人被新诊断出患有精神分裂症是极其罕见的。

sentences.en: Which raises the possibility that he was getting these diagnoses because that was a routine way that these nursing homes handled patients with dementia.
sentences.zh: 这就引发了一种可能性，即他之所以被诊断出这些病，是因为这是这些疗养院处理痴呆症患者的常规方式。

sentences.en: They just wanted to sedate them.
sentences.zh: 他们只是想让他镇静下来。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And, you know, as the lawyer started going through his medical records,
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，随着律师开始仔细审阅他的病历，

sentences.en: he and his team found that there were several people at the home who started to raise questions about the medications that he was getting and the effect that they were having on his health.
sentences.zh: 他和他的团队发现，疗养院里有几个人开始对给他服用的药物以及这些药物对他的健康产生的影响提出疑问。

sentences.en: Like what?
sentences.zh: 比如什么？

sentences.en: What were some of the questions that he raised?
sentences.zh: 他提出的有哪些问题？

sentences.en: Well, for example, a physical therapist who was seeing him in the medical records said that she was having a hard time doing her work because he was sleeping all of the time.
sentences.zh: 嗯，例如，病历显示，一位为他看病的物理治疗师说，她很难开展工作，因为他一直在睡觉。

sentences.en: You know, in kind of one memorable record, she talks about actually using a washcloth to try and wake him up but not being successful.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，在其中一份令人印象深刻的记录中，她谈到实际上用毛巾试图唤醒他，但没有成功。

sentences.en: You know, another time a dietician, you know, he was losing weight very quickly.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，另一次是一位营养师，你知道的，他体重下降得非常快。

sentences.en: You know, he lost at 1.12 pounds in a single week.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他在短短一周内就瘦了 1.12 磅。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: And the dietician actually wrote a note to the doctor asking him to consider adjusting his medications because she said he was sleeping all day through his meals.
sentences.zh: 营养师实际上给医生写了一张便条，请他考虑调整他的药物，因为她说他整天都在睡觉，饭都顾不上吃。

sentences.en: So he wasn't, you know, waking up enough to eat.
sentences.zh: 所以他，你知道的，没有醒来足够的时间来吃东西。

sentences.en: And perhaps most notably,
sentences.zh: 也许最引人注目的是，

sentences.en: an outside pharmacist whose job is to review the medications that nursing home residents are getting raises concerns about Haldol and another antipsychotic that he was getting and writes in a note to the nursing home doctor that was treating Mr. Blakeney and said,
sentences.zh: 一位外部药剂师，其职责是审查疗养院居民正在服用的药物，对氟哌啶醇以及他正在服用的另一种抗精神病药物提出了担忧，并在给治疗布莱克尼先生的疗养院医生的便条中写道，

sentences.en: you know, hey, you should taper him off of these drugs.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，嘿，你应该让他逐渐停用这些药物。

sentences.en: And the pharmacist actually referred back to that 2005 FDA warning, you know, about being really careful about using these drugs in older patients.
sentences.zh: 药剂师实际上回顾了 2005 年美国食品药品监督管理局（FDA）的警告，即在老年患者中使用这些药物时要非常小心。

sentences.en: And so on this form, there's a box for the doctor to check and that box is checked disagree.
sentences.zh: 因此，在这个表单上，有一个供医生勾选的方框，该方框勾选了不同意。

sentences.en: And then there's a note below it that says staff feels need,
sentences.zh: 然后下面有一条便条，写着员工觉得有必要，

sentences.en: which seemed to also call back to that early Ronald Reagan era law that warned nursing homes against giving patients drugs to meet the needs of the staff and not the needs of the patient.
sentences.zh: 这似乎也让人回想起罗纳德·里根时代早期的法律，该法律警告疗养院不要为了满足员工的需求而不是病人的需求而给病人服药。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对的。

sentences.en: The whole point was that this was not supposed to be about staff needs, but about what was best for Blakeney.
sentences.zh: 重点是，这不应该关乎员工的需求，而应该关乎对布莱克尼最有利的事情。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So after this doctor overrules the pharmacist, what happens next?
sentences.zh: 那么在这位医生否决了药剂师之后，接下来发生了什么？

sentences.en: Well, over the next several months, you know, despite the concerns that were raised by these different people, Mr. Blakeney continues getting Haldol and other drugs.
sentences.zh: 嗯，在接下来的几个月里，你知道的，尽管这些人提出了担忧，布莱克尼先生仍然继续服用氟哌啶醇和其他药物。

sentences.en: And his condition continues to decline.
sentences.zh: 他的病情继续恶化。

sentences.en: He goes in and out of the hospital for a variety of reasons.
sentences.zh: 由于各种原因，他频频进出医院。

sentences.en: And, you know, finally, it is June of 2017 and Mrs. Blakeney decides that she has to intervene.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，终于到了 2017 年 6 月，布莱克尼太太决定她必须进行干预。

sentences.en: Did you want to move him because of the care he was getting?
sentences.zh: 你想搬走他是因为他得到的护理吗？

sentences.en: No, I knew they wasn't taking care of him.
sentences.zh: 不，我知道他们没有照顾他。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: They was not taking care of him.
sentences.zh: 他们根本没有照顾他。

sentences.en: Sometimes when you go, there would be nobody there.
sentences.zh: 有时候你去了，那里一个人也没有。

sentences.en: You know, it was like real people there.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，就像那里有真正的人一样。

sentences.en: In the whole nursing home.
sentences.zh: 在整个疗养院里。

sentences.en: In the whole nursing home and people crying and hollering, who's going to change me?
sentences.zh: 在整个疗养院里，人们在哭喊，谁来帮我换衣服？

sentences.en: Who's going to feed me?
sentences.zh: 谁来喂我吃饭？

sentences.en: And there wasn't nobody there to feed him.
sentences.zh: 而且没有人去喂他。

sentences.en: And she starts looking around for a different nursing home that will take him.
sentences.zh: 于是她开始四处寻找一家愿意接纳他的不同的疗养院。

sentences.en: And so finally, she finds a different home.
sentences.zh: 最后，她找到了一家不同的疗养院。

sentences.en: And she gets him settled into the new place.
sentences.zh: 她把他安顿在了一个新的地方。

sentences.en: But, you know, by then, David Blakeney is out of time.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道的，到那时，大卫·布莱克尼已经时日无多。

sentences.en: I tried my best, though, to get in my butt.
sentences.zh: 不过，我尽力了，想融入其中。

sentences.en: It was too late.
sentences.zh: 太迟了。

sentences.en: Katie, I'm curious if you have called the nursing home where David Blakeney spent the most time
sentences.zh: 凯蒂，我很好奇你是否打电话给大卫·布莱克尼度过时间最长、

sentences.en: and had this terrible decline and what they have said to you about what happened to him.
sentences.zh: 病情极度恶化的那家疗养院，他们对发生在他身上的事情对你说了什么？

sentences.en: I called them several times.
sentences.zh: 我给他们打过好几次电话。

sentences.en: I sent emails.
sentences.zh: 我发过电子邮件。

sentences.en: I reached out to their lawyer.
sentences.zh: 我联系了他们的律师。

sentences.en: And they did not respond to my request for comment.
sentences.zh: 他们没有回应我的置评请求。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: David died in 2017.
sentences.zh: 大卫死于 2017 年。

sentences.en: Before the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 在疫情爆发之前。

sentences.en: And listening to you describe this long history of what has happened to nursing home patients,
sentences.zh: 听你描述疗养院患者所经历的这段漫长历史，

sentences.en: I'm wondering if COVID-19 has made the problems that you have been describing worse.
sentences.zh: 我在想，新冠疫情是否使你一直在描述的问题变得更加严重。

sentences.en: You know, many people that I spoke to who, you know, spend a lot of time in nursing homes say that there's several factors about the pandemic that likely made the use of these
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我交谈过的许多人，你知道的，在疗养院里度过了很长时间，他们说疫情的几个因素可能使这些抗精神病药物的使用变得更加糟糕。

sentences.en: antipsychotics worse.
sentences.zh: 抗精神病药物。

sentences.en: You know, first of all, there's a desperate staffing crisis right now.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，首先，现在存在严重的人手危机。

sentences.en: And we know that when there are fewer staffs, you know, there's been several studies that show that they're more likely to use antipsychotics.
sentences.zh: 我们知道，当员工较少时，你知道的，有多项研究表明他们更有可能使用抗精神病药物。

sentences.en: In addition, there is a need in an infectious outbreak to keep problematic patients in their rooMs.
sentences.zh: 此外，在传染病爆发期间，需要将有问题的患者留在房间里。

sentences.en: And, you know, it is very challenging behavior to have a patient with dementia who's wandering around when there's active COVID spreading in your nursing home.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，当疗养院里正在广泛传播新冠疫情时，让患有痴呆症并四处游荡的患者表现出极具挑战性的行为。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: So both of those factors, not enough staffing, a need to keep these residents socially distant,
sentences.zh: 所以这两个因素，人手不足，需要让这些居民保持社交距离，

sentences.en: you're saying would incentivize the abuse of these drugs.
sentences.zh: 你是说这会助长滥用这些药物的行为。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And in fact, when we looked at the data, that is what we found, is that there actually has been an uptick in the use of antipsychotic drugs during the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 事实上，当我们查看数据时，我们发现的情况确实如此，即在疫情期间，抗精神病药物的使用确实有所上升。

sentences.en: Katie, what would a nursing home, a typical nursing home, look like if drugs like Haldol were
sentences.zh: 凯蒂，如果像氟哌啶醇这样的药物没有按照你所发现的那种方式、

sentences.en: not being prescribed in the way that you have found they are, on the scale that you have found they are, what would they look like, feel like?
sentences.zh: 在你所发现的那种规模下被开处方，那么一家疗养院，一家典型的疗养院，会是什么样子，感觉会是什么样？

sentences.en: You know, there's many nursing homes that have successfully reduced their use of antipsychotics
sentences.zh: 你知道的，有许多疗养院已经成功减少了抗精神病药物的使用，

sentences.en: and found, you know, a lot of alternatives that, you know, that don't include giving them drugs to kind of helping manage these patients and these residents' behavior.
sentences.zh: 并且发现，你知道的，有很多替代方案，你知道的，这些方案不包括给他们喂药来帮助管理这些患者和这些居民的行为。

sentences.en: But, you know, it takes resources, it takes staffing, and it takes a lot of other things that many, many nursing homes don't have.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道的，这需要资源，需要人员，还需要许多其他很多很多疗养院所没有的东西。

sentences.en: So this decades-long battle to curtail the use of these antipsychotic drugs and this kind of incorrect diagnosis of schizophrenia has pretty clearly failed.
sentences.zh: 因此，这场长达数十年的减少使用这些抗精神病药物以及这种错误诊断精神分裂症的斗争显然已经失败了。

sentences.en: But I have to say that this seems to be a much larger problem here, which is with the entire nursing home industry and how we care or don't care enough for people in this country
sentences.zh: 但我必须说，这里似乎存在一个更大得多的问题，那就是整个疗养院行业，以及我们如何关爱或不够关爱这个国家临近生命终点的人。

sentences.en: nearing the end of their lives.
sentences.zh: 生命即将走到尽头。

sentences.en: And during the pandemic, nursing homes became the great villains because so many people died there.
sentences.zh: 在疫情期间，疗养院成了声名狼藉的大恶人，因为那里有太多人死亡。

sentences.en: And now your investigation is adding a new dimension to the problems at nursing homes.
sentences.zh: 现在你的调查为疗养院的问题增添了新的维度。

sentences.en: So when we think about that whole industry, are we talking about a flawed system or, at this point, an entirely broken system?
sentences.zh: 因此，当我们审视整个行业时，我们讨论的是一个有缺陷的系统，还是在这一点上，一个完全破碎的系统？

sentences.en: You know, there's a lot of people that when they talk about the nursing home system in our country, they would describe it as broken or, you know, in need of a complete overhaul.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，有很多人在谈论我们国家的疗养院系统时，会将其描述为破碎的，或者，你知道的，需要彻底大修。

sentences.en: One reason is, is that, you know, the majority of nursing homes in this country are for-profit businesses.
sentences.zh: 原因之一是，你知道的，这个国家的绝大多数疗养院都是营利性企业。

sentences.en: And that for-profit nursing home industry would also tell you that they're operating on extremely thin profit margins.
sentences.zh: 那些营利性疗养院行业也会告诉你，他们的运营利润空间极小。

sentences.en: They're not getting paid enough to properly staff their facilities and give their nursing homes the resources that they need.
sentences.zh: 他们的报酬不足以使其设施配备足够的人员，并为其疗养院提供所需的资源。

sentences.en: But I think almost everyone would agree that just caring for our older people in this country is, is just simply not a priority.
sentences.zh: 但我认为几乎每个人都会同意，照顾这个国家的老年人，根本就不是优先事项。

sentences.en: And it's often really overlooked, which is really tragic because, you know, pretty much all of us are going to get there sometime.
sentences.zh: 而且它经常被真正忽视，这真是一个悲剧，因为，你知道的，几乎我们所有人终有一天都会走到那一步。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对的。

sentences.en: And we all have family members who are affected by this.
sentences.zh: 我们所有人的家庭成员都有可能受到这件事的影响。

sentences.en: So it affects everyone.
sentences.zh: 所以这关乎每个人。

sentences.en: You know, if, if we're lucky, we'll grow old.
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果，如果我们幸运的话，我们都会变老。

sentences.en: And, um, the question is, you know, how will we be cared for when we are old?
sentences.zh: 然后，嗯，问题是，你知道，当我们老了的时候，谁来照顾我们？

sentences.en: Katie, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 凯蒂，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: We appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我们非常感激。

sentences.en: Thanks so much for having me.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢邀请我来。

sentences.en: What message do you want people to take from your husband's story?
sentences.zh: 你希望大家从你丈夫的故事中领悟到什么信息？

sentences.en: Like what, what do you, what would you want people to learn from it?
sentences.zh: 比如什么，你觉得，你希望人们从中学到什么？

sentences.en: If you can take care of your mother, your father, whatever.
sentences.zh: 如果你能照顾你的母亲、父亲，无论是什么人。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I would have never put him in there.
sentences.zh: 我绝不会把他送到那种地方去。

sentences.en: Never.
sentences.zh: 绝不。

sentences.en: Don't just throw your parents away.
sentences.zh: 不要就这样抛弃你们的父母。

sentences.en: Don't put them in there.
sentences.zh: 别把他们送进那种地方。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to another day.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要了解的内容。

sentences.en: The people of Afghanistan need a lifeline.
sentences.zh: 阿富汗人民需要一条生命线。

sentences.en: After decades of war, suffering and insecurity, they face perhaps their most perilous hour.
sentences.zh: 经历了几十年的战争、苦难和动荡之后，他们或许正面临最危险的时刻。

sentences.en: On Monday, the United Nations warned of a humanitarian crisis in Afghanistan, saying that millions of Afghans could run out of food before the arrival of winter.
sentences.zh: 周一，联合国对阿富汗的人道主义危机发出警告，称数百万阿富汗人可能在冬天到来之前面临断粮。

sentences.en: Speaking at a conference devoted to the crisis, the UN Secretary General said that since the Taliban's takeover,
sentences.zh: 联合国秘书长在一次专门讨论这场危机的会议上表示，自从塔利班接管以来，

sentences.en: Afghanistan's poverty rate has soared and basic public services are nearing collapse.
sentences.zh: 阿富汗的贫困率急剧飙升，基础公共服务濒临崩溃。

sentences.en: And let us be clear, this conference is not simply about what we will give to the people of Afghanistan.
sentences.zh: 我们要明确一点，这次会议不只是关于我们要向阿富汗人民提供什么。

sentences.en: It is about what we owe.
sentences.zh: 而是关于我们亏欠他们什么。

sentences.en: And House Democrats have released a plan to raise more than $2 trillion by taxing the income of high-earning individuals and profitable corporations.
sentences.zh: 众议院民主党人公布了一项计划，拟通过对高收入个人和盈利企业的收入征税来筹集超过2万亿美元。

sentences.en: But the Times reports that the plan does not tax the wealth of the nation's ultra-rich, whose fortunes have soared over the past decade,
sentences.zh: 但《纽约时报》报道称，该计划并未对国家超级富豪的财富征税——在过去十年里，这些人的财富激增，

sentences.en: and does not close the most egregious tax loopholes that they exploit.
sentences.zh: 而且也没有堵住他们所利用的那些最恶劣的税收漏洞。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Asla Chaturvedi, Lindsay Garrison, and Stella Tan.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由阿斯拉·查图维迪、林赛·加里森和斯特拉·陈制作。

sentences.en: It was edited by Dave Shaw and contains original music by Alishaba Etoop and Dan Powell and engineered by Alishaba Etoop.
sentences.zh: 由戴夫·肖剪辑，原创音乐由阿里沙巴·埃图普和丹·鲍威尔创作，并由阿里沙巴·埃图普负责混音工程。

sentences.en: Our theme music is by Jim Brunberg and Ben Lansford of Wonderly.
sentences.zh: 我们的主题曲由Wonderly乐队的吉姆·布伦伯格和本·兰斯福德创作。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是本期《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Ibarra.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·伊巴拉。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine, until this summer, when elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直像一个被严密控制的机器一样运作，直到今年夏天，选举迎来了一批自称为改革派的人士。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党就陷入了一场残酷、混乱、有时又令人兴奋的权力之争。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro, with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在《都市》最新一期节目中，我是主持人莎拉·凯尼格，我们将讲述人们试图维持影响力却在过程中逐渐失控的故事。

sentences.en: Metro.
sentences.zh: 《都市》。

sentences.en: Listen wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 请在各大播客平台收听。
